items.question: What is A1, A2, B1, B2, C1, C2 in German?
items.answer:
A1 to C2 are German proficiency levels based on the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR).

  • A1: You can use simple German expressions, introduce yourself, ask basic questions, and manage simple everyday interactions.
  • A2: You can communicate about familiar topics such as family, work, shopping, and routine activities.
  • B1: You can communicate more independently, talk about experiences, express opinions, and understand the main ideas of standard German.
  • B2: You can communicate more confidently, understand detailed conversations, discuss complex topics, and use German in professional or academic contexts.
  • C1: You can communicate fluently and effectively in a wide range of professional, academic, and social situations.
  • C2: You can understand and communicate German with a very high level of fluency, accuracy, and precision.

Fluent AUF offers German learning programs from A1 to C2.

items.question: Can I learn German in 3 months?
items.answer:
Three months of consistent learning can help you develop a useful foundation in German. The progress you make depends on your starting level, practice time, and consistency.

For beginners, a focused three-month learning plan can help build an A1-level foundation. Regular classes, daily speaking practice, vocabulary building, German audio and video content, reading, writing, and mock tests can all contribute to steady improvement.

Levels A1, A2, B1, and B2 are used to classify the proficiency in the German language according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages.

  • A1: Beginner - Understand and use basic German phrases; introduce yourself, ask simple questions, and perform everyday tasks.
  • A2: Elementary - Communicate in familiar situations, understand simple dialogues, and speak about familiar topics, like family, work, shopping, and so on.
  • B1: Intermediate - Be able to communicate independently in familiar situations, express your opinion, tell about experiences, and understand the general meaning of the standard German.
  • B2: Upper-Intermediate - Speak fluently and confidently; communicate about complex topics, understand detailed conversations, and apply the German language for professional and academic purposes.

You can learn German from A1 to C2 at our organization Fluent AUF.

items.question: Can I learn A1 German in 2 weeks?
items.answer: Yes, you can learn the basics of A1 German in 2 weeks, but becoming fully comfortable at A1 level in that time is difficult. With intensive daily practice, you can build a foundation in greetings, basic grammar, vocabulary, sentence formation, and everyday conversations. For a stronger A1 level and exam readiness, most learners need several weeks of consistent classes and self-study.

items.question: What is A1, A2, B1, B2 German?
items.answer:
Levels A1, A2, B1, and B2 are used to classify the proficiency in the German language according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages.

  • A1: Beginner - Understand and use basic German phrases; introduce yourself, ask simple questions, and perform everyday tasks.
  • A2: Elementary - Communicate in familiar situations, understand simple dialogues, and speak about familiar topics, like family, work, shopping, and so on.
  • B1: Intermediate - Be able to communicate independently in familiar situations, express your opinion, tell about experiences, and understand the general meaning of the standard German.
  • B2: Upper-Intermediate - Speak fluently and confidently; communicate about complex topics, understand detailed conversations, and apply the German language for professional and academic purposes.

You can learn German from A1 to C2 at our organization Fluent AUF.

items.question: Is 3 months enough to learn German?

Regular German classes combined with speaking practice, vocabulary development, and self-study can help you understand basic German and communicate in common everyday situations.

To improve your German effectively, you can:

  • Attend German classes consistently.
  • Practice speaking German every day.
  • Learn and revise new vocabulary regularly.
  • Listen to German podcasts, videos, and other audio content.
  • Practice reading and writing in German.
  • Take mock tests to track your progress and identify areas for improvement.

items.question: What is A1, A2, B1, B2 German?
items.answer:
Levels A1, A2, B1, and B2 are used to classify the proficiency in the German language according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages.

A1: Beginner - Understand and use basic German phrases; introduce yourself, ask simple questions, and perform everyday tasks.

A2: Elementary - Communicate in familiar situations, understand simple dialogues, and speak about familiar topics, like family, work, shopping, and so on.

B1: Intermediate - Be able to communicate independently in familiar situations, express your opinion, tell about experiences, and understand the general meaning of the standard German.

B2: Upper-Intermediate - Speak fluently and confidently; communicate about complex topics, understand detailed conversations, and apply the German language for professional and academic purposes.

You can learn German from A1 to C2 at our organization Fluent AUF.
